report.source_text: Laboratory workup included a complete blood count, compressive metabolic panel, coagulation profile, urinalysis, and serum lactic acid testing, which were found to be unexceptional except for an elevated lactate of 9.2 mmol/L as well as an elevated serum creatinine of 1.14 mg/dL, with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 53 mL/minute/1.73m2. Urinalysis demonstrated moderate leukocyte esterase with microscopy showing 12 white blood cells and three red blood cells per high-power field.

report.source_text: Due to the amount of perinephric and periureteric fluid present, the decision was made to obtain delayed CT imaging to exclude ureteral injury. CT with delayed images obtained after contrast injection revealed extravasation of contrast from the left proximal as well as mid-ureter (Figure 2).

report.source_text: The patient then underwent placement of a double-J stent with Foley catheter placement. The patient was discharged with oral antibiotics and outpatient follow-up for repeat cystoscopy and evaluation for possible stent removal in one month.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old woman presented with acute severe left flank pain, nausea, vomiting, and left costovertebral angle tenderness. Initial CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast showed left kidney edema, collecting system dilation, and perinephric/periureteric fluid without obstructing stone. Labs demonstrated mild renal impairment, sterile pyuria, and elevated lactate. Delayed CT imaging confirmed contrast extravasation from the left proximal and mid-ureter indicating ureter rupture. Cystoscopy with retrograde pyelogram confirmed ureter rupture 2 cm distal to the ureteropelvic junction with no stones or other causes. The patient was treated with IV antibiotics, fluids, cystoscopy, double-J stent placement, and Foley catheter, followed by discharge on oral antibiotics and scheduled outpatient follow-up.
